crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
children.blurb: Local and air-gapped model deployment covers running AI models on hardware the organization controls, from a workstation under a desk to a rack in a private data center, with no dependency on a public API.

children.name: Secure Storage and Networking for Legal Data
children.blurb: Secure storage and networking for legal data covers the systems and controls that hold and move client files, matter documents, privileged communications, contracts, discovery material, and case strategy.

children.name: Timekeeping and Billing Narratives
children.blurb: Timekeeping and billing narratives cover the written descriptions that lawyers and paralegals attach to billable time, along with the systems and rules that turn those entries into client invoices.

children.name: Firm Knowledge Management
children.blurb: Firm knowledge management covers the internal know-how a law firm creates and reuses, including precedents, clause banks, matter files, research memos, deal documents, and profiles of who knows what.

children.name: Client Intake and Triage
children.blurb: Client intake and triage covers the first structured contact between a prospective client and a legal team, including identity capture, conflict screening, matter description, urgency assessment, and routing to the right practice group.

sections.body: This section covers the operational plumbing that lets a law office actually run AI tools rather than just talk about them. Local and air-gapped deployment means running a model on hardware the firm controls, sometimes with no outside network connection at all, which matters when client material cannot leave the building. Secure storage and networking covers how that data is held, encrypted and moved between machines and offices. Timekeeping and billing narratives is the least glamorous and most used: turning rough notes about a matter into the descriptive entries that invoices require. Firm knowledge management is the internal search and drafting layer over a firm's own work product, and client intake and triage is the front door, where enquiries get sorted, conflicts checked and matters routed. None of this is theoretical. Firms are running local models on workstations and small servers, and they are pointing retrieval systems at their own document stores today.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The deployment side is genuinely workable now. Open weight models run on a single well specified machine, and air-gapped setups are a real option for practices that cannot send data to a vendor. Secure storage and networking is mostly ordinary security engineering with AI specific wrinkles, chiefly that prompts and retrieved passages become new copies of sensitive material that need the same controls as the originals. Billing narrative generation works well as a drafting aid and poorly as an autonomous one, because a plausible sounding entry that misstates the work is a billing problem, not a writing problem. Knowledge management succeeds when the corpus is clean and permissioned and fails when it is not, and permission inheritance across a document store remains the hard part. Intake and triage can classify and summarise enquiries, but conflict checking and the judgement calls stay with people. The honest limits are data quality, access control and the fact that a wrong output in this section costs money or confidentiality rather than just time.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment to understand what hardware and model choices are available when data cannot leave the firm, since that decision constrains everything else here. Secure Storage and Networking for Legal Data follows directly, covering how the resulting prompts, embeddings and documents are protected in transit and at rest. From there, Timekeeping and Billing Narratives is the most immediately practical page for anyone who bills by the hour, and it is the clearest example of AI as a drafting aid rather than a decision maker. Firm Knowledge Management is the larger and slower project, and it depends on the storage and permission work described earlier. Client Intake and Triage sits at the other end of the matter lifecycle, handling what arrives before any of the internal systems see it. Read together, the five pages describe a single pipeline from first contact to final invoice, with security running underneath all of it.
